summary: Friedrich Weller specialized in Indology, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his Dr. phil. and Habilitation at Leipzig University, studying under August Conrady, and later held teaching posts there (~1922-1928, 1938-1958) and membership in the Saxon Academy of Sciences.

Friedrich Wilhelm was an Indologist and Tibetologist who completed his doctorate at the University of Munich and studied under Paul Thieme. He served as Privatdozent at Munich, was affiliated with the Bavarian Academy, and held visiting professorships at Columbia and the Collège de France.
Friedrich Wilhelm Graf is a religious studies scholar. He held academic posts at the University of Augsburg (~1989-1999) and the University of Munich (~1999-2014).

Friedrich Wilhelm Joseph Schelling was a philosopher who studied at the Tübinger Stift, Tübingen, and Leipzig. He held professorships at Jena (1798-1803), Würzburg (1803-1806), Erlangen-Nuremberg (1820-1827), Munich (1827-1841), and Berlin (1841-1845), and led the Bavarian Academy of Sciences.
Friedrich Wilhelm Karl Müller worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied under Georg von der Gabelentz and Karl Foy, and later taught Yinke Chen.

Friedrich Wilhelm Ritschl was a scholar of linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at Leipzig and Halle-Wittenberg, he held posts at Halle (~1829-1833), Breslau (1834), the University of Bonn (1839), and Leipzig University (~1865-1875).

Friedrich Windischmann was an Indologist and Iranian studies scholar. He studied at Bonn under Lassen, Schlegel, Welcker, Niebuhr, Brandis, and K. J. H. Windischmann, and at Munich. He held posts at Munich, Freising, and the Archdiocese of Munich and Freising.

Friedrich von Adelung worked in Indology, linguistics, history, and archaeology. After studying at Leipzig University (1787-1790), he held honorary professorships at Kharkiv and Tartu (1809), and administrative posts at the University of Vienna (1824) and Utrecht University (1825).

Friedrich von Schlegel was an Indologist, linguist, and philosopher. He studied at Göttingen under Heyne, at Leipzig, and in Paris under Alexander Hamilton and de Chézy. He later taught at the universities of Jena (1800), Cologne (1804), and TU Dresden (1828).

Friedrich von Spiegel was an Iranian and Indology scholar. He studied at Erlangen, Leipzig, Bonn, and Jena under Brockhaus, Rückert, Fleischer, Kinkel, and Lassen. He served as professor of Oriental languages at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from 1849 to 1891.

Frits Staal worked in Indology, philosophy, and linguistics. He studied at Amsterdam, Madras, and Banaras Hindu University. He held positions at Amsterdam, SOAS, the University of Pennsylvania, and served as professor at the University of California, Berkeley (1968-1991).
Fritz Johaentgen was an Indologist who studied under Christian Lassen and Martin Haug.

Fritz-Joachim von Rintelen was a philosopher who studied and completed his Habilitation at the University of Munich. He held professorships at Bonn (1934), Munich (1936-1941), and Mainz (~1947-1969), alongside visiting posts at Córdoba, UCLA, Tokyo, and Chicago.

Frédéric Baudry was a scholar of linguistics and Indology who studied under Eugène Burnouf. He held librarian and administrative posts at the Institut agronomique de Versailles, Bibliothèque de l'Arsenal, and Bibliothèque Mazarine, and was a member of the Académie des Inscriptions.

Fu-shih Lin was a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and history. He completed graduate studies at Princeton University under Ying-shih Yü, Denis Twitchett, and Stephen F. Teiser, and held a long-term post at Academia Sinica (~1994-2021).
Fuang Jotiko was a Buddhist studies figure who studied under Ajahn Lee Dhammadharo and Mun Bhuridatta, and later taught Ṭhānissaro Bhikkhu.
Fuguan Xu worked in philosophy, Sinology, and history. He studied at Meiji University and under Shili Xiong, and later served on the faculty at Tunghai University (~1955-1969).
Fujio Oda is a history and archaeology scholar who studied at Kyushu University (~1952-1960). He held academic posts at Beppu University (~1967-1974) and Fukuoka University (~1974-2004).

Fujio Taniguchi specializes in Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology. He earned his PhD at Nagoya University under Musashi Tachikawa, studied under several other teachers, and has held affiliations with Nagoya Women's University, Aichi Gakuin University, and the Eastern Institute.

Fumi Yao is a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology who holds appointments as associate professor at the University of Tokyo, part-time lecturer at Taisho University, and is affiliated with the Eastern Institute.
